{{nihongo|'''Kota Shrine'''|居多神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Echigo Province]].

=== Company name ===
The company name ``Ita'' is an old notation that can be found in various documents including ``{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}'' and {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Shinmyocho}}. Regarding Kun, it appears to be ``keta'' in the ``Jingishiryo'', ``eta'' in the Kujo family book, Takeda family book, and Yoshida family book, and ``kota'' in ``{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō Studies|Q11588824|qid=Q11588824}}'', but it is currently read as ``kota'' {{Sfn|Etsusa Shrine|2002|p=14-15}}. Keta Shrine located along the coast of the Sea of Japan (Disambiguation)|Q11548075|Keta Shrine}} It is said that it was called ``Keta'' in ancient times, and it is thought that it was not called ``Kota'' or ``Ita'' until later times.

In addition, there is an ancient example of reading ``ke'' as ``ke'' on a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=iron sword excavated from the Inariyama Tumulus}} dating back to the end of the 5th century {{Sfn|Ichinomiya system in medieval countries|2000|p=368-369}}.

=== Enshrined God ===
The following four deities are currently enshrined. group="Note">In the explanation board in the precincts, the enshrined deities are listed as 3 deities: Okuninushi no Mikoto, Nunagawahime no Mikoto, and Takeminakata no Mikoto, and in the shrine statement book of 1883, they are listed as 3 deities: Ōkuninushi no Mikoto, Nunagawa Hime no Mikoto, and Jishironushi no Mikoto. {{Harv|Ichinomiya system in medieval countries|2000|p=368-369}}. </ref>. 
* {{ill|Ōkuninushi|Q276944|qid=Q276944|lt=Ōkuninushi}} (Ookuninushi no Kami)
* {{ill|Nunakawahime|Q11142832|qid=Q11142832|lt=Nunagawa Hime-kami}} (Nunagawa Himenokami) - Also known as ``Numakawa Hime'' in literature. Wife of Okuninushi.
* {{ill|Takeminakata|es|Takeminakata|hu|Takeminakata|id|Takeminakata|ja|タケミナカタ|mni|ꯇꯀꯦꯃꯤꯅꯀꯇ|pl|Takeminakata|zh|建御名方神|qid=Q9150391|lt=Takeminakata no kami}} (Takeminakata no kami) - Son of Okuninushi no kami.
* {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|fa|کوتوشیرونوشی|fr|Kotoshironushi|it|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主|ko|고토시로누시|ru|Котосиронуси|simple|Kotoshironushi|th|โคโตชิโรนูชิ|zh|事代主神|qid=Q8009611|lt=Kotoshironushi no Kami}} (Kotoshironushi Mikami) - Son of Okuninushi.

This Ketakami is said to be a god worshiped by the people of Izumo, and is said to be the god of Takashi Province ({{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ekoku}}; Similar to the story of the marriage of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Nunagawa Hime no Mikoto}} in the current Hokuriku region, the distribution of Ketakami is thought to tell the story of the advance of the Izumo force into the Hokuriku region.{{Sfn|Ita Shrine (Gods)|1985}}.

=== Outline ===
According to the documents in the shrine's collection (according to the legend "{{ill|Nihon Kōki|Q1077029|qid=Q1077029}}" Itbun), 4 years ago ({{ill|Kōnin (era)|Q1373070|qid=Q1373070}} ({{ill|813|Q30360|qid=Q30360}}, the {{ill|Shinkai (divine rank)|Q11591025|qid=Q11591025}} of ``Itagami'' was promoted from no rank to junior fifth rank, and after that, the divine rank was {{jalink|jogan}. (Japan)|Q1075635|Jokan}} Promoted to Junior Fourth Rank Lower in 3rd year ({{ill|861|Q23913|qid=Q23913}}) {{Sfn|Ita Shrine (Heibonsha)|1986}}.{{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274|lt=Extended}} 5 years ({{ill|927|Q30470|qid=Q30470}}) "{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}" {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Shinmyocho}} is described as "Ita Shrine" in {{ill|Echigo Province|be|Этыго (правінцыя)|ckb|پارێزگای ئێچیگۆ|cs|Provincie Ečigo|de|Provinz Echigo|es|Provincia de Echigo|fa|ولایت اچیگو|fr|Province d'Echigo|gl|Provincia de Echigo|id|Provinsi Echigo|it|Echigo|ja|越後国|ko|에치고국|lt|Ečigo žemė|nl|Echigo (provincie)|pt|Província de Echigo|ru|Этиго (провинция)|simple|Echigo Province|sk|Ečigo (provincia)|sr|Провинција Ечиго|tr|Echigo (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Етіґо|zh|越後國|zh_min_nan|Etigo-kok|zh_yue|越後國|qid=Q666514}}{{ill|Kubiki district|ja|頸城郡|qid=Q11664982}}, and is listed as {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}}{{Sfn|Ita Shrine (Heibonsha)|1986}}. Also, "{{ill|Chōya Gunsai|Q11517735|qid=Q11517735}}" in {{ill|Jōryaku|Q279743|qid=Q279743}}4 ({{ill|1080|Q19448|qid=Q19448}}) In the June 10th article, it appears to be listed as "Keta Shrine" and also {{Sfn|Ita Shrine (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Ichinomiya system in medieval countries| 2000|p=368-369}}, according to the company biography, in the first year of {{ill|Jōgen (Kamakura period)|Q1194389|qid=Q1194389}} ({{ill|1207|Q5232|qid=Q5232}}) It is said that when {{ill|Shinran|Q512934|qid=Q512934}} was exiled to Echigo Kokufu, he visited Ita Shrine {{Sfn|Ita Shrine (Gods)|1985}}.{{ill|Nanboku-chō period|Q264012|qid=Q264012|lt=After the Nanbokucho period}}, Ida Shrine was revered by the guardian {{ill|Uesugi clan|Q1150058|qid=Q1150058|lt=Uesugi family}}. {{Sfn|Ita Shrine (Heibonsha)|1986}} is said to have been located in {{ill|Ichinomiya|ca|Ichinomiya (Xinto)|de|Ichi-no-miya|fr|Ichi-no-miya|id|Ichinomiya|ja|一宮|ko|이치노미야|pt|Ichinomiya (templo)|simple|Ichinomiya|th|อิจิโนมิยะ|uk|Ітіномія (титул)|zh|一宮|qid=Q1656379}} of k|Echigo Province|Q666514}}. The historical documents that identify Ita Shrine as a shrine were first seen in the documents held by Ita Shrine dated 3rd year ({{ill|1347|Q6082|qid=Q6082}}), and are also found here and there in other Ita Shrine documents and Uesugi family documents.{{Sfn|Ita Shrine (Heibonsha)|1986}}. On the other hand, among the shrines known as Ichinomiya in Echigo Province, there is {{ill|Yahiko Shrine|Q195684|qid=Q195684}} in {{ill|Yahiko, Niigata|Q1349667|qid=Q1349667}} {{Sfn|Ichinomiya system in medieval countries|2000|p=365}}. The details of the development of the Ichinomiya system in Echigo are not clear, but it is believed that Yahiko Shrine was actually an Ichinomiya shrine, although the name "Ichinomiya" itself was not used until the Heian period. There is a theory that Niita Shrine gained the reverence of the Uesugi family and officially called itself Ichinomiya, and Yahiko Shrine also began to call it Ichinomiya {{Sfn|Ichinomiya System in Medieval Countries|2000|p=365}}.In the 3rd year of Teiwa (1347), the shogunate granted Taiho for repair costs, and in 1351 |Q6104}}) Aramakiho was donated by Echigo Shugo {{ill|Uesugi Noriaki|Q11359188|qid=Q11359188}} {{Sfn|Ita Shrine (Heibonsha)|1986}}. Also {{ill|Bunmei|Q1193544|qid=Q1193544|lt=Bunmei}} In the 18th year ({{ill|1486|Q6646|qid=Q6646}}), {{ill|Gyōe|Q11464814|qid=Q11464814}} of Joko-in Temple in Kyoto ("Northern Travels"), Ink|1488|Q4853}}), {{ill|Banrishūku|Q11353943|qid=Q11353943}}, a monk in Kyoto {{ill|Shōkoku-ji|Q1786709|qid=Q1786709}}, visits Ita Shrine (``Baika Mujinzo'') {{Sfn|Ita Shrine (Gods)|1985}}. According to "Hokugoku Kiko," a priest named ``Nagasaki (Hanaga-mae)'' was in charge of the shrine's affairs, and it says that Ita-jinja became a new deity to protect the North Sea from the time of {{ill|Empress Jingū|Q232803|qid=Q232803}}'s {{ill|Three Han Campaign|Q11249435|qid=Q11249435}} {{Sfn|Ita Shrine (Gods)|1985}}. The Hanagamae clan, the priest of this shrine, is said to have been an influential zaisho who descended to Echigo Province as appointed Kokushi {{Sfn|Ichinomiya system in medieval countries|2000|p=365}}, and has continued to hold the Shinto priesthood to this day.{{ill|Sengoku period|Q204023|qid=Q204023|lt=Sengoku period}}, it was involved in wars, and {{ill|Tenbun|Q1192853|qid=Q1192853|lt=Tenbun}} In 2nd year ({{ill|1533|Q6443|qid=Q6443}}), the shrine building was burnt down by {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Sadanori Uesugi}}, and in the same year In 1986, the Shugodai {{ill|Nagao Tamekage|Q909963|qid=Q909963}} prayed for the destruction of Sadanori Uesugi and others and promised to rebuild the shrine.{{Sfn|Ita Shrine (Heibonsha)|1986}}. Also, after the death of {{ill|Uesugi Kenshin|Q311080|qid=Q311080}}, a succession dispute ({{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Otate Rebellion}}), the shrine was attacked by the {{ill|Uesugi Kagetora|Q1190934|qid=Q1190934}} side and was attacked by the {{ill|Uesugi Kagekatsu|Q1376605|qid=Q1376605}} side, and the shrine building was burned down.{{Sfn|Ita Shrine (Heibonsha)|1986}}. At this time, the priest Hanagamae Morisada and Iemori father and son fled abroad, and Morisada died abroad, but Iemori returned to Japan after Kagekatsu's transfer to Aizu and when {{ill|Hori Hideharu|Q9755540|qid=Q9755540}} entered {{ill|Kasugayama Castle|Q1197131|qid=Q1197131}} {{Sfn|Ita Shrine (Heibonsha)|1986}}.In {{ill|Keichō|Q1328185|qid=Q1328185}}4 ({{ill|1599|Q6803|qid=Q6803}}), Hideharu Hori granted 13 koku as shrine territory, and {{ill|Edo period|lt=Edo period|qid=Q184963}} In the 16th year of the Keicho era ({{ill|1611|Q6768|qid=Q6768}}), the shogunate granted 100 koku as nienz|zea|1866|zh|1866年|zh_classical|一八六六年|zh_min_nan|1866 nî|zh_yue|1866年|qid=Q7712}}), the shrine grounds of Mt.Minowa were {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=coastal erosion}}, it was destroyed by {{Sfn|Ita Shrine (Heibonsha)|1986}}, and the divine spirit was transferred to the chief priest's house and enshrined there {{Sfn|Meiji Shrine Journal |1912}}. After {{ill|Meiji Restoration|Q8707|qid=Q8707}}, in May of {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}}5 ({{ill|1872|Q7753|qid=Q7753}}), {{ill|Q712534|lt=Modern Company Ranking System}} It was ranked as {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}} in May 1873, and was promoted to {{ill|Ken-sha|lt=prefectural shrine|qid=Q90139226}} in May 1873|1912}}. In the 12th year of the Meiji era ({{ill|1879|Q7783|qid=Q7783}}), a shrine building was built at the current location and the shrine was relocated{{Sfn|Meiji Shrine Archives|1912}}. This shrine building was destroyed by fire in 1902 ({{ill|1902|Q2043|qid=Q2043}}), and a temporary shrine building was built in 40th year of Meiji ({{ill|1907|Q2048|qid=Q2048}}) {{Sfn|Ita Shrine (Heibonsha)|1986}}. After that, the main building was built in June 2008 ({{ill|Heisei era|ar|فترة هيسي|br|Oadvezh Heisei|ca|Període Heisei|cdo|Bìng-sìng|ckb|سەردەمی ھێیسێی|cs|Období Heisei|de|Heisei-Zeit|eo|Hejsej-epoko|es|Era Heisei|fa|دوره هیسه‌ای|fi|Heisei-kausi|fr|Ère Heisei|he|תקופת הייסי|hi|हेइसेई युग|hr|Heisei|hu|Heiszei-kor|id|Zaman Heisei|it|Periodo Heisei|ja|平成|ka|ჰეისეის პერიოდი|ko|헤이세이 시대|lt|Heisei laikotarpis|ms|Zaman Heisei|nl|Heiseiperiode|no|Heisei|oc|Heisei|pl|Heisei|pt|Período Heisei|ru|Хэйсэй|sco|Heisei period|simple|Heisei era|sk|Obdobie Heisei|sl|Heisei (obdobje)|su|Heisei|sv|Heisei|th|ยุคเฮเซ|tl|Panahong Heisei|tr|Heisei Dönemi|uk|Хейсей|uz|Heisei|vi|Thời kỳ Bình Thành|zh|平成|zh_classical|平成|zh_min_nan|Pêng-sêng|zh_yue|平成|qid=Q234510}}) and remains there today.

=== God level ===
Record of divine investiture in {{ill|Rikkokushi|Q1151168|qid=Q1151168}}. Both are written as ``Itagami''.
* {{ill|Kōnin (era)|Q1373070|qid=Q1373070}} July 4th year ({{ill|813|Q30360|qid=Q30360}}), from no rank to junior fifth rank (an excerpt from ``{{ill|Nihon Kōki|Q1077029|qid=Q1077029}}'' from the ``Jingi Hakusodehan Iita Shrine Iki Certificate'' owned by Ida Shrine) <ref group="Note">Articles that appear to be "Nihon Koki" in Ita Shrine documents. In "Nihon Koki," the article written in July of the 4th year of Konin is missing, and the credibility of the article is said to be high even when compared with the article of the 3rd year of Jogan. </ref>
* {{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jogan}}3rd year ({{ill|861|Q23913|qid=Q23913}}) August 3rd, from the top of the fifth rank to the bottom of the fourth rank (``{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Q1052981|qid=Q1052981}}'')

In the precincts, {{ill|Phragmites australis|Q28557|qid=Q28557|lt=reeds}} ``single-leaf reeds'' grow in clusters {{Sfn|Ita Shrine (Gods)|1985}}. Legend has it that when Shinran visited Ita Shrine and prayed, the reeds in the shrine grounds became single leaves overnight {{Sfn|Ita Shrine (Gods)|1985}}. This single-leaf reed is also counted as one of the "{{ill|Seven Wonders of Echigo|Q11636487|qid=Q11636487}}"{{Sfn|Ita Shrine (Gods)|1985}}.

=== Setsusha ===
* Karita Shrine - Enshrined deity: {{ill|Takamimusubi|UNKNOWN|Takamimusubi|lt=Kōnosūreishin|qid=Q125400}}, {{ill|Kamimusubi|UNKNOWN|Kamimusubi|lt=Shinsōsōreishin|qid=Q3275901}}<ref name="Explanation board">Precinct explanation board. </ref>
* Inari Shrine - Enshrined Deity: {{ill|Ukanomitama|de|Ukanomitama|eo|Ukanomitama|fr|Uka-no-Mitama|ja|ウカノミタマ|mni|ꯎꯀꯅꯣꯃꯤꯇꯃ|ru|Ука-но митама|simple|Ukanomitama|sv|Ukanomitama|th|อูกาโนมิตามะ|zh|宇迦之御魂神|qid=Q3080728|lt=Kurainatama-no-Mikoto}}<ref name="Explanation board"/>

Until 1866, six shrines were enshrined within the precincts of the former shrine: Tenjin Shrine, Yawata Shrine, Inari Shrine, Yasaka Shrine, Suwa Shrine, and Oma Shrine.

=== Festival ===
Main festivals held at Ita Shrine {{Sfn|Ita Shrine (Gods)|1985}}.
* Annual festival (May 3rd)
* Grand Festival (August 19th and 20th)
* Niinamesai (November 23rd)
